result.title: Compositional neural networks for multimodal X-ray and neutron scattering inversion
result.summary: X-ray and neutron scattering are indispensable for structural characterization across condensed-matter physics and materials science. Yet, because scattering experiments generally record intensities without phase information, distinct structures can yield similar scattering patterns, rendering the corresponding inverse problems non-unique. This ambiguity can be reduced by combining complementary measurements, but their integration into machine-learning frameworks remains challenging. Here we introduce a modular framework for probabilistic multi-measurement analysis based on prior-amortized flow matching. Single-observation posterior estimators are trained separately for individual observation types or physical probes and combined only at inference time through a compositional sampler. This late fusion approach allows pretrained single-observation models to be reused without dedicated joint retraining. As a case in point, we consider reflectometry, which provides depth-resolved, nanometer-scale information about thin films and interfaces. Our single-observation demonstrations span X-ray, time-of-flight neutron and polarized neutron reflectometry. In separate co-refinement studies, task-matched estimators enable homogeneous composition across multiple neutron contrasts and heterogeneous multimodal composition of X-ray and neutron measurements. Together, these results establish compositional flow matching as a modular approach to uncertainty-aware inversion and co-refinement, with potential applicability to other scattering problems in which multiple observations constrain a common physical structure while retaining measurement-specific parameters.

AI.brief_summary: 提出基于先验摊销 flow matching 的模块化概率反演框架：为 X 射线、中子等单类观测分别训练后验估计器，仅在推理时用组合采样器融合，实现不联合重训的共精修与不确定性量化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「推理期组合多源证据后验、共享物理结构但保留各自参数」的后期融合思路，可能与 LVR 中多视觉证据筛选、证据整合与何时停止取证的决策问题构成概念类比，可供核查，但与原论文的 VLM 推理无直接联系。
